CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is the North Musi Rawas Regency.
2. Regency Government is the North Musi Rawas Regency Government.
3. Regent is the North Musi Rawas Regent.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Office of Village Community Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Office, is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in North Musi Rawas Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, as well as mother and her children, and persons who are their dependents.
11. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
12. Guardian is a person or entity who in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child.
13. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
14. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields.
15. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to victims.
16. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world, which is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and protection.
17. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a Regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years counted from inauguration until the end of the Regent's term of office.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Annual Financial Plan of Regional Government established by Regional Regulation.
19. Regional Action Plan is a document containing policies, programs and activities in order to realize objectives in accordance with regional authority.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the government or community-based.
21. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.

CHAPTER VIII
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 43
Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Part Two Rights of the Child
Article 10
Every Child has the right to live, grow, develop, and participate appropriately in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as to receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Article 17
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
(2) Every Child has the right to receive protection in educational institutions from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 36
Legal services as referred to in Article 31 letter e are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation which includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to completely describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Second Part
Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence

Article 29
(1) The Regency Government, in implementing the Protection of Women and Children, shall be coordinated by the Service/Office.
(2) The Regency Government, in implementing the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1), may establish P2TP2A.
(3) Further provisions regarding P2TP2A shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 23
Every Child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence and sexual discrimination, or who is in conflict with the law, has the right for their identity to be kept confidential.

CHAPTER IV IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
First Part
General

CHAPTER V
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 39
(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Children Protection.
(2) The Regent, in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), may delegate it to the Regional Apparatuses.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be coordinated with the Service (Dinas).

Article 21
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain protection from being the target of persecution, torture, or the imposition of inhumane punishment.
(2) Every Child has the right to obtain freedom in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Arrest, detention, or criminal imprisonment of a Child shall only be carried out as a last resort in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 22
Every Child who becomes a perpetrator or victim of a criminal act has the right to:
a. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
b. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal proceedings; and
c. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial Children's court in a closed session to the public.

1.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines “Keluarga” (Art. 1(10)) and mentions protection being carried out by “pihak keluarga” (Art. 1(8)), but it never explicitly frames or names “kekerasan dalam rumah tangga” (domestic violence) / intimate partner violence as a distinct category. The retrieved English passages likewise only speak generally about “violence against women and children” (e.g., Art. 26, 27, 31) without a domestic/household qualifier. The judge’s rationale (no explicit domestic violence category) matches the text; therefore the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be an over-labeling.

1.5.evaluator_rationale: Although the definition of violence includes “economic” and the child protection provisions mention “economic exploitation” and “neglect,” the criterion requires economic violence/exploitation or domestic neglect specifically as a form of violence against women; the provided sentences only specify exploitation/neglect in relation to children, not women.

1.5.rationale: The Indonesian definition of “Kekerasan” includes “ekonomi” (Art. 1(15): ‘fisik, seksual, ekonomi, sosial, psikis’), which is a general definition applicable to victims (women and/or children). However, the regulation does not specifically enumerate economic violence against women (it enumerates women’s rights and empowerment, and for children it explicitly mentions ‘eksploitasi, baik ekonomi maupun seksual’ in Art. 14(b)). If the indicator requires explicit economic violence/exploitation as a form of violence against women (as the judge assumed), the document does not clearly do that. Given the retrieved passages include the general definition with “economic,” a ‘Yes’ could be arguable under a broader interpretation, but the golden label ‘Yes’ seems inconsistent with the document’s lack of explicit women-focused economic violence provisions; thus the golden label is likely the problem.

1.6.translated_snippet: c. prevent the occurrence of marriage at the age of a Child;
1.6.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly addresses prevention of child marriage, which is a harmful practice affecting girls.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is the North Musi Rawas Regency.
2. Regency Government is the North Musi Rawas Regency Government.
3. Regent is the North Musi Rawas Regent.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Office of Village Community Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Office, is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in North Musi Rawas Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, as well as mother and her children, and persons who are their dependents.
11. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
12. Guardian is a person or entity who in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child.
13. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
14. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields.
15. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to victims.
16. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world, which is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and protection.
17. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is a Regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years counted from inauguration until the end of the Regent's term of office.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Annual Financial Plan of Regional Government established by Regional Regulation.
19. Regional Action Plan is a document containing policies, programs and activities in order to realize objectives in accordance with regional authority.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the government or community-based.
21. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.

Second Part
Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence

CHAPTER IV IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
First Part
General

CHAPTER VIII
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 43
Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 29
(1) The Regency Government, in implementing the Protection of Women and Children, shall be coordinated by the Service/Office.
(2) The Regency Government, in implementing the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1), may establish P2TP2A.
(3) Further provisions regarding P2TP2A shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER II
RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
Rights of Women

CHAPTER V
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 39
(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Children Protection.
(2) The Regent, in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), may delegate it to the Regional Apparatuses.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be coordinated with the Service (Dinas).

Article 40
(1) Supervision as referred to in Article 39 is implemented through monitoring and evaluation of:
a. policies/programs for the Protection of Women and Children; and
b. implementation of activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
(2) The results of monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically to the Regent.

Article 36
Legal services as referred to in Article 31 letter e are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation which includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to completely describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 9
(1) The implementation of Women's empowerment in the field of law as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) may be implemented through:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) The implementation of Women's empowerment in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 35
(1) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 31 letter d constitute services provided in order to restore victims from a traumatic condition.
(2) The form of services as referred to in paragraph (1) is through social support.
(3) Social support as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out through:
a. spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.

CHAPTER VI
FINANCING
Article 41
Financing for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children is sourced from:
a. APBD; and/or
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 32
Complaint, consultation, and counseling services as referred to in Article 31 letter a include:
a. identification or initial recording of victims;
b. case identification; and
c. consent for action to be taken.

Article 21
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain protection from being the target of persecution, torture, or the imposition of inhumane punishment.
(2) Every Child has the right to obtain freedom in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Arrest, detention, or criminal imprisonment of a Child shall only be carried out as a last resort in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

6.2.rationale: The Indonesian definition of P2TP2A explicitly includes protection from violence/discrimination ‘termasuk perdagangan orang’ (including trafficking in persons) (Art. 1(20)). This indicates trafficking is within the scope of services for women and children. The judge’s ‘Yes’ is directly supported by the source text shown to the judge. Therefore the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.

6.5.evaluator_rationale: The policy provides specific additional rights for children with disabilities (e.g., special education, rehabilitation, social assistance), which constitutes special measures targeted at persons with disabilities within the policy’s framework (though focused on children rather than women with disabilities).
